web_title: 6. 10-Year Financial Forensics, Cash Conversion & Balance Sheet
book_title: Chapter 6: The Forensic Ledger — Ten Years of Profit, Cash & Capital Allocation
question: What do ten years of audited GAAP financials (FY2017–FY2026) and H1 FY2027 results reveal about Cirrus Logic's true growth rate, cash conversion, ROIC, balance sheet strength, and buyback efficacy?

epigraph.quote: Net income is an accounting opinion shaped by write-downs and tax timing; ten-year cumulative free cash flow minus dilution is the financial truth.
epigraph.author: Forensic Accounting Principle

web_blocks.title: 6.1 10-Year Audited GAAP Income Statement & Cash Flow Forensics (FY2017–FY2026)

web_blocks.html: Ten full years of audited Form 10-K filings (FY2017 through FY2026, ending late March) show the core trade-off in Cirrus Logic [1][13]. Top-line growth has been slow and bumpy. Sales rose from $1,538.94 million in FY2017 to $1,997.38 million in FY2026—a 2.9% 9-year CAGR (and a 7.8% 5-year CAGR off the FY2021 COVID base of $1,369.23 million) [1][13]. Yet per-share earnings grew nearly three times faster than sales. GAAP diluted EPS doubled from $3.92 in FY2017 to $7.85 in FY2026 (+8.0% 9-year CAGR; +16.7% 5-year CAGR) [1][13]. Three clean levers drove that gap: 353 basis points of gross margin gain (49.2% to 52.8%), tight opex control (EBIT margin up from 20.6% to 23.0%), and a 20.6% drop in diluted shares via cash buybacks [1][13].

web_blocks.caption: Cirrus Logic: 10-Year Audited GAAP Financial Forensics (FY2017 – FY2026, $ Millions except EPS & %)
web_blocks.takeaway: *FY2023 GAAP EBIT and Net Income reflect an $85.76M Lion Semiconductor intangible write-down and $10.63M in restructuring [9]. Over ten years, Cirrus Logic generated $3.22 billion in FCF—133.5% of GAAP Net Income—while spending just 1.8% of sales on capex [1][13].

web_blocks.title: 6.2 Latest Interim Trajectory: H1 FY2027 & Q3 FY2027 Outlook

web_blocks.html: In H1 FY2027 (six months ended September 26, 2026), Cirrus Logic posted $1,019.19 million in sales, up 5.3% YoY from $968.23 million [2][4]. GAAP gross margin rose 70 basis points YoY to 53.2% [2][4]. Still, opex rose 11.8% YoY to $325.60 million due to R&D hiring (up to 1,815 staff) and $6.9 million in Q2 deal costs [2][3]. That kept H1 GAAP EBIT flat at $216.81 million (vs. $217.16 million) and GAAP net income flat at $191.59 million (vs. $192.29 million) [2][3]. Thanks to buybacks (diluted shares fell 3.0% YoY to 51.48 million in Q2), H1 GAAP diluted EPS still rose 2.2% YoY to $3.69 [2][4]. For Q3 FY2027 (December quarter), management guided sales to $510 million–$570 million (-7% YoY at the midpoint) and GAAP gross margin to 51%–53%. GAAP opex steps up to $184 million–$190 million, including ~$21 million SBC and ~$9 million in deal costs [3]. Higher near-term spend plus a softer December guide confirm FY2027 is an investment phase. That gap between top-line growth and flat near-term EBIT is worth tracking closely. Higher R&D spend funds calendar 2028 camera and AI PC ramps, yet it trims near-term operating leverage while December sales cool [2][3].

web_blocks.title: 6.3 Cash Conversion, ROIC & Balance Sheet Fortress Audit

web_blocks.html: Cirrus Logic's cash conversion ranks among the cleanest in chips. From FY2017 through FY2026, operating cash flow totaled $3,520.86 million against $2,413.59 million in GAAP net income. That is a 145.9% ten-year CFO-to-Net-Income ratio [1][13]. The lone soft cash year was FY2022 ($124.75 million CFO). That dip came from the $195.0 million GlobalFoundries wafer prepayment and a post-COVID receivables build, and the cash came back in full across FY2024–FY2026 [1][9]. Ten-year capex totaled just $298.20 million, or 1.8% of sales. As a result, ten-year Free Cash Flow hit $3,222.66 million, a 19.8% average FCF margin [1][13].

The balance sheet is an unlevered fortress. On March 28, 2026 (FY2026 end), cash and marketable securities hit $1,153.79 million against $0 in funded debt [1]. That cash split into $800.93 million in cash and equivalents, $86.70 million in short-term securities, and $266.16 million in long-term securities [1]. Total liabilities of $361.38 million were mostly $133.98 million in operating leases, $80.65 million in payables, and accrued pay and taxes [1]. At Q2 FY2027 end (September 26, 2026), cash and securities stood at $1,076.43 million ($720.12 million cash, $31.92 million ST, $324.39 million LT) with zero funded debt [2][3]. The slight dip reflected seasonal receivables and $125.5 million in Q2 buybacks [2][3]. Equity stood at $2,128.00 million at FY2026 end and $2,192.17 million at Q2 FY27 [1][2]. True operating ROIC is elite: FY2026 NOPAT ($460.38M EBIT × (1 - 0.166) = $383.96M) over ~$1,108M average operating capital yields ~34.7% operating ROIC. Even counting the full $1.15 billion idle cash pile, headline ROIC is ~18.0% [1].

web_blocks.title: 6.4 Stock-Based Compensation (SBC) vs. Share Repurchases Forensic Check

web_blocks.html: In fabless tech firms, always test if buybacks shrink the share count or merely offset stock-based pay. Cirrus Logic passes this test cleanly [1][13]. From FY2017 through FY2026, GAAP SBC totaled $651.80 million, averaging 4.0% of sales and 20.2% of FCF ($81.81 million or 4.1% of sales in FY2026) [1][13]. Over the same decade, Cirrus spent $1,667.07 million on share buybacks—2.56x cumulative SBC [1][13]. Diluted shares fell steadily from 66.56 million in FY2017 to 52.82 million in FY2026 (-20.6%), and down to 51.48 million in Q2 FY2027 (-22.7% vs. FY2017) [1][2][13]. On October 26, 2026, the Board added a $500 million buyback plan on top of $114.1 million left at Q2 end, keeping net share retirements rolling [2][3]. For long-term holders, that buyback track record is a major anchor. Cash generation consistently retires real shares rather than leaking away into executive pay dilution [1][13].

web_blocks.caption: Cirrus Logic: 10-Year SBC Dilution vs. Share Repurchase Audit (FY2017 – FY2026 & Q2 FY2027)
web_blocks.takeaway: Unlike peers whose buybacks merely offset SBC, Cirrus Logic spent 2.56x its 10-year SBC on buybacks. It cut over one-fifth of its share count while building a $1.1B+ cash pile [1][2][13].

web_blocks.title: Price-Blind Business Quality Synthesis: Why CRUS Is CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL
paragraphs: Set market narratives aside, and the audited ten-year ledger tells a sharp two-sided story. On economics, Cirrus Logic is a rare fabless gem: 51%–53% gross margins, 146% ten-year CFO-to-net-income conversion, and >34% operating ROIC. It also holds zero debt, over $1.08 billion in cash and securities, and a 22.7% lower share count since FY2017 [1][2][13].

On structure, however, a 2.9% nine-year sales CAGR and 91%–93% reliance on Apple rule out an autonomous compounder tag [1][2][13]. Business quality is strictly CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL: an elite cash engine whose long-term durability still rests on phone socket retention and future non-phone scale.

book_paragraphs: Numbers do not lie when you read ten years of them in a single column. If you and I lay Cirrus Logic's audited financial statements from fiscal 2017 through fiscal 2026 side by side, two competing truths jump off the page immediately—and understanding both of them is the entire secret to underwriting this company honestly.

Truth number one is that top-line growth has been surprisingly sluggish and cyclical. Back in fiscal 2017, Cirrus Logic generated $1.54 billion in revenue. Nine years later, in fiscal 2026, revenue reached $2.00 billion. That works out to a compound annual revenue growth rate of just 2.9 percent—and along the way, you had to stomach a brutal 22.6 percent revenue drop in fiscal 2019 and a 5.7 percent dip in fiscal 2024. This is not a hyper-growth software rocket ship; it is a mature, cyclical hardware supplier.

Truth number two, however, is that Cirrus Logic's financial engine beneath the top line is remarkably disciplined. Over those exact same nine years, GAAP diluted earnings per share doubled from $3.92 to $7.85—compounding at 8 percent a year, nearly three times faster than sales. How do you double EPS when revenue grows under 3 percent a year? By expanding gross margins from 49.2 percent to 52.8 percent, holding SG&A lean, converting 146 percent of net income into operating cash flow, and relentlessly shrinking the share count.

book_subsections.title: The Ten-Year Cash Machine and the Unlevered Fortress
paragraphs: Look at the cash flow statement across the full decade from fiscal 2017 through fiscal 2026. Cirrus Logic reported $2.41 billion in cumulative GAAP net income—and converted that into $3.52 billion in operating cash flow. Because a fabless chip designer needs very little physical equipment, ten-year cumulative capital expenditures were just $298 million—less than 2 percent of total sales. That left $3.22 billion in pure Free Cash Flow over the decade, or roughly 20 cents of free cash out of every single revenue dollar!

Look what that cash built on the balance sheet. Exiting fiscal 2026, Cirrus Logic held $1.15 billion in cash and marketable securities ($1.08 billion at the end of September 2026 after seasonal receivables and buybacks) against zero financial debt. Even if you penalize its return on invested capital by leaving that entire billion-dollar cash hoard inside the denominator, Cirrus earns an 18 percent headline ROIC; measure it on the actual operating capital required to run the business, and operating ROIC exceeds 34 percent.

book_subsections.title: Testing Buybacks Against Stock-Based Compensation
paragraphs: Whenever a tech company boasts about buying back stock, you and I always run one simple forensic test: are they actually shrinking the pie for remaining owners, or are they just sweeping up executive stock-based compensation? Over the past ten fiscal years, Cirrus Logic issued $652 million in stock-based compensation—about 4 percent of revenue. Over that exact same decade, it spent $1.67 billion repurchasing its own shares—more than two-and-a-half times its SBC. As a result, the diluted share count has marched downward every single year like clockwork, falling from 66.6 million shares in fiscal 2017 to 52.8 million in fiscal 2026 and 51.5 million in Q2 FY27—a genuine 22.7 percent reduction in shares outstanding.

Put all six chapters together without peeking at a single stock quote, and our unbiased verdict writes itself. Cirrus Logic is financially elite—debt-free, cash-rich, high-ROIC, and disciplined with shareholder capital—yet structurally constrained by a 2.9 percent nine-year sales CAGR and a 91 to 93 percent reliance on Apple. That is the textbook definition of a CYCLICAL_CONDITIONAL franchise: wonderful economics while its flagship sockets hold, demanding strict discipline whenever we eventually examine what the market is asking us to pay for it.

book_subsections.title: Reading the Latest H1 FY2027 Numbers and the FY2027 Investment Phase
paragraphs: Before we close the ledger on Pass 1, let's zoom in on the freshest audited and unaudited numbers from the first half of fiscal 2027, ended September 26, 2026. First-half revenue rose 5.3 percent year over year to $1.019 billion, driven entirely by an 11.1 percent surge in HPMS sales while Audio held flat. GAAP gross margin expanded 70 basis points to 53.2 percent—peaking at 53.7 percent in the September quarter thanks to favorable product mix and that temporary prior-contract GlobalFoundries wafer benefit.

Yet look closely at the operating-profit line: despite $51 million of extra revenue in the first half, GAAP operating income was completely flat at $216.8 million (versus $217.2 million a year earlier), and GAAP net income held flat at $191.6 million. Why? Because management is leaning heavily into an investment cycle—hiring engineers to 1,815 total headcount, absorbing $6.9 million of acquisition-related costs in Q2 (with another $9 million projected in Q3), and funding tape-outs for the fourth-generation camera controller, the second-generation AI PC codec, and the 3D-sensing smart power IC. Meanwhile, Q3 FY27 revenue guidance of $510 million to $570 million implies a 7 percent year-over-year decline at the midpoint as smartphone shipment timing normalizes and PC delays linger.

Notice how consistent this picture is with our ten-year forensic verdict. Cirrus Logic has the balance sheet ($1.08 billion in cash and marketable securities, zero debt) and the cash-flow discipline ($500 million fresh buyback authorization) to invest right through a flatter fiscal 2027 without blinking. That financial strength is genuine and rare. At the same time, flat near-term operating profits, 93 percent quarterly customer concentration, and a sub-3 percent nine-year revenue growth rate mean we should never mistake a disciplined cash cow for an unstoppable secular compounder. Holding both of those truths simultaneously is what prepares us to look at price and valuation with completely clear eyes.

book_callouts.title: Mentor Check: The Two Numbers to Remember Before Pass 2
book_callouts.text: As we close our price-blind business audit, lock two facts into memory: Cirrus Logic generated $3.22 billion in free cash flow over ten years with zero debt and shrank its share count by nearly 23%—yet one customer still supplies 91%–93% of sales. That tension is the exact lens we will carry into valuation.
